points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (each node has at most two children, left and right).
States the ordering property: for any node, the left child (left subtree) is smaller than the parent, and the parent is smaller than the right child (right subtree). Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: 1.5 marks if only one side of the ordering is stated correctly (left smaller or right larger), or the ordering is vague, e.g. 'sorted' without left/right.

rubric.notes: Full marks: identifies a binary tree and gives the left < parent < right ordering at every node. Part marks: only the binary tree structure, or only a partial or vague ordering. No marks: answers that describe other structures or give no ordering or structure.
